justification: The ~541 prompts and their rule-based, auto-checkable verification functions are fully open on the HF dataset (google/IFEval) and GitHub since the Nov 2023 release with no refresh since; generic instruction-following (word counts, keywords, formatting) is heavily represented in pretraining and RLHF data, and by 2024-2026 frontier models were already near-saturated on it.

Ai2 released the full 58-constraint test set and verification code on HF (allenai/IFBench_test) and GitHub as a fixed set, not periodically rotated; it was purpose-built to hold out constraint types unseen during typical IFEval-style RLVR training, so individual questions generalize less well to memorization even though the set itself is public and static.

Full English/Chinese datasets and constraint-evolution paths are open on GitHub/HF with no updates since the Nov 2023 (v2) paper; the multi-level incremental-constraint-stacking structure (up to 5 compounding constraints per instruction) is a less common training signal than single-constraint IFEval-style data, though the underlying constraint types themselves are ordinary.

The 80 questions have been public in the FastChat GitHub repo since June 2023 with no rotation; open-ended multi-turn chat-quality Q&A is one of the most heavily represented data types in modern chat-model post-training, and GPT-4-era models were already scoring near the 10-point ceiling in the original paper itself.

The 805 test instructions and reference model outputs are public in the tatsu-lab/alpaca_eval GitHub repo (length-controlled win-rate vs. a fixed GPT-4-Preview-1106 baseline), unchanged since introduction; general single-turn instruction-following/chat quality is extremely well represented in pretraining and RLHF data, and the repo's own leaderboard has gone stale since Dec 2024, consistent with saturation.

The released WildBench set (HF allenai/WildBench) is a fixed, one-time curated sample of real Chatbot Arena user queries, not periodically refreshed (the HF Space itself went inactive after Aug 2024); sourcing from real, diverse in-the-wild user traffic gives broader task-type coverage than hand-curated benchmarks, though the frozen released set can still be scraped/memorized once public.

Scale AI runs MultiChallenge as a hosted, continuously-scored leaderboard (scale.com/leaderboard/multichallenge) rather than releasing a full public answer key, consistent with Scale's general private-eval pattern (seen explicitly in MCP-Atlas's public/private task split); it targets multi-turn instruction retention, inference memory, and self-coherence across conversation turns, a structurally harder/less-memorizable target than single-turn win-rate.

Berkeley's dataset, eval harness, and versioned test categories (v1-v4) are fully open on GitHub, and the 'Live' function-calling categories are explicitly sourced from ongoing community/user contributions and periodically expanded (v4 added Web Search and Memory categories in 2025), unlike a one-time-frozen set; function/tool-calling schemas are moderately represented in pretraining but the newer agentic categories (web search loops, KV/vector/recursive-summarization memory) are less so.

Sierra open-sourced the full dual-control environment, task generator, and grading code on GitHub, and has actively extended it (new telecom/banking-knowledge/voice domains and a v1.0.1 grading update through 2026), with Artificial Analysis independently re-running it against new model releases over time; the dual-control paradigm (both agent AND simulated user can act on a shared, stateful world) is a genuinely novel interaction structure with little precedent in standard pretraining or single-control agent benchmarks.

Scale AI explicitly splits the 1,000 tasks into 500 public (released on HF as ScaleAI/MCP-Atlas) and 500 held-out private tasks used for official leaderboard scoring, and the task set itself has not been described as periodically refreshed; evaluating tool discovery/parameterization across 36 real, current MCP servers with deliberately placed distractor tools is a recent (2025-2026) evaluation paradigm with minimal representation in any model's pretraining data.

The full 16,000+-API dataset, ToolLLaMA training data, and ToolEval code have been open on GitHub/HF since 2023 with no updates found since (the repo's changelog stops before 2024); real-API tool-use framed as ReACT/DFSDT tool call sequences is now a well-represented pattern in agentic post-training data, and the benchmark has been effectively superseded by BFCL in current citation frequency.

MINT-Bench (ICLR 2024) is explicitly built by repurposing existing, extremely well-known public datasets (GSM8K, HotpotQA, MATH, MMLU, HumanEval, MBPP, ALFWorld) into a multi-turn tool-and-feedback wrapper; the wrapper/interaction structure is somewhat novel but the underlying question content itself is heavily memorized/public, and no live leaderboard update was found beyond the original paper.

Salesforce released the CRMArena-Pro paper, code, and a Hugging Face results leaderboard, but it is unclear from available sources whether the underlying synthetic Salesforce-CRM task/data generation seeds are fully public or partly held out for grading integrity; realistic enterprise CRM workflows (business-process policy compliance, confidentiality handling, multi-turn case resolution) are a domain with comparatively little representation in general-purpose pretraining corpora.
